questions.question: Drukpa Tsechi, a festival celebrated in Sikkim, is associated with which of the following personalities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Buddha.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **According to the English Calendar, **it falls somewhere around **July or August each year in Sikkim**. Coming to the legend behind the festival,** it is observed to celebrate Lord Buddha and his first preaching of the Four Noble Truths.**
 
• Drukpa Tsheshi is celebrated on the 4th day (Tsheshi) of the 6th month (Drukpa) of the Tibetan Calendar in Sikkim.
 
• This preaching was granted to his five disciples at the Deer Park in Sarnath.
 
 
• The** first noble truth acquaints with suffering.**
 
• The second noble** truth acclaims the truth of the origin of the suffering, accident, chance, illusion, and their causes.**
 
• The** third noble truth confirms the termination of suffering or the realization of 'Nirvana'.**
 
• The** fourth noble truth says about the truth of the Eight Fold Path, which eventually leads to Nirvana.​**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Festivals**
 **Associated with personality**
 
 

 
 
 
• **Mahavir Jayanti **is one of the most significant festivals among the Jain community and is celebrated with splendour in India and across the world. **The festival commemorates the birth of Lord Mahavira.**
 
 
 **Lord Mahavira**
 
 

 
 
 
• Hindus across the world are celebrating **Diwali,** to mark the** return of Lord Rama to his kingdom Ayodhya with his wife Sita and his brother Lakshmana **after defeating Ravana in Lanka and serving 14 years of exile. The festival celebrates the victory of light over darkness. 
 
 
 **Lord Rama**
 
 

 
 
 
• **Janmashtami** is a Hindu festival celebrating** the birth of the god Krishna **on the eighth (Ashtami) day of the dark fortnight of the month of Bhadrapada (August–September)
 
 
 **Lord Krishna**

questions.question: Which of the following rivers originates at Trimbakeshwar in Maharashtra?

• The **Hindu belief is that those who visit Trimbakeshwar attain salvation or Moksha.**
 
• Trimbakeshwar is considered the most sacred town in India.
 
• The Godavari originates from the Brahmagiri hills in this town and it is believed that it is the birthplace of **Lord Ganesha, known as a place of Tri-Sandhya Gayatri.**
 
• This place is believed to be the holiest and ideal place to do the Shraddha ceremony, a Hindu ritual for the salvation of the soul.
 
• A shraddha on the river Godavari gives great satisfaction to the forefathers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**​

• The** total length of the river** from origin to its outfall into the Bay of Bengal is **1,400 km.**
 
 
 
• **Damodar river**
 
 
• The Damodar River** rises in the Palamau hills of Chota Nagpur **at an **elevation of about 609.75 m**.
 
 
 
• **Mahanadi river**
 
 
• ​The river** Mahanadi originates at an elevation of about 422 mts. **above mean sea level** near Pharsiya village near Nagri town in Raipur district of Chhattisgarh.**

questions.question: The Reserve Bank of India also acted as the central bank for _______ till April 1947.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Burma.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Burma (Myanmar) seceded from the Indian Union in 1937** but the **Reserve Bank continued to act as the Central Bank for Burma till the Japanese Occupation of Burma and later up to April 1947.**
 
• After the partition of India,** the Reserve Bank served as the central bank of Pakistan up to June 1948 **when the State Bank of Pakistan commenced operations.
 
• The RBI was originally set up as a shareholder's bank and was nationalized in 1949.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Reserve Bank of India was **set up on the basis of the recommendations of the Hilton Young Commission.**
 
• **The Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934** provides the statutory basis for the functioning of the Bank, which** commenced operations on April 1, 1935.**
 
• The Reserve Bank of India is the central bank of the country.
 
• The function of the bank include 
 
 
• **Monetary Policy.**
 
• **Bank Supervision and Regulation.**
 
• **Overseeing the Payments System and developing the financial markets.**

questions.question: The ancient port, Sopara is located in which of the following state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sopara was an ancient port town** and the capital of the ancient Aparanta **(Western Border) **in **western Maharashtra.**
 
• In ancient times, it was the** largest township on India's west** coast,** trading with Mesopotamia, Egypt, Cochin, Arabia and Eastern Africa.**
 
• The** site of this ancient town i**s located** near the present-day Nala Sopara town in the Thane district**, now in the newly created** Palghar district of Maharashtra, India.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__ **

 
• Ancient ports of India
 
• **Lothal Port**
 
 
• **The oldest port in India,** Lothal was an important port **city of the Indus valley civilization **and was located in today’s Bhal region of Gujarat.
 
• Existed about 4500 years ago,** and the remains of the port city of Lothal were discovered in 1954.**
 
 
 
• **Muziris Port**
 
 
• **Muziris, the ancient port city located in today’s Indian state of Kerala**, was one of the most important trading ports in the world almost 2,000 years ago.
 
• **Existed in the first century BC, the Muziris port had played a significant role in connecting the region with the Persians, the Phoenicians, the Assyrians, the Greeks, the Egyptians and the Roman Empire.**
 
• While **spices, particularly black pepper, were the key item exported from the Muziris port. **
 
 
 
• **Arikamedu Port**
 
 
• **Arikamedu, located in today’s Puducherry,** a union territory of India, is known as the port of Podouke in historical documents.
 
• **Arikamedu is believed to be an active trading port of the region with the Roman Empire** as early as the second century BC.

questions.question: Which one of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution directs the State to ensure the right of citizens to adequate means of livelihood?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 39**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 39 (a) of the Constitution,** enunciated as one of the Directive Principles, requires the State to direct its policies towards **securing that all its citizens have the right to an adequate means of livelihood.**
 
• Article39, states certain principles of policy to be followed by the State:
 
• The State shall, in particular, direct its policy toward securing
 
 
• that the citizens,** men, and women equally, have the right to an adequate means of livelihood.**
 
• that the** ownership and control of the material resources** of the community are so distributed as best to **subserve the common good.**
 
• that the operation of the economic system** does not result in the concentration of wealth** and means of production to the common detriment.
 
• that there is** equal pay for equal work for both men and women.**
 
• that** children are given opportunities and facilities to develop in a healthy manner** and in conditions of freedom and dignity and that childhood and **youth are protected against exploitation **and against moral and material abandonment.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Articles 36-51 under Part-IV of the Indian Constitution deal with Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).**
 
• They are** borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland.**
 
• They** seek to establish economic and social democracy** in the country.
 
• **DPSPs** are ideals that **are not legally enforceable **by the courts for their violation.

questions.question: In June 2020, who among the following was appointed as the chairman of the National Institute of Public Finance and Policy (NIPFP)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Urjit Patel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Urjit Patel, the former governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI),** has been named chairman of the **National Institute of Public Finance and Policy (NIPFP),** a Delhi-based research institution that works closely with governments on policy reforms.
 
• Three representatives from the Ministry of Finance, one from the Planning Commission of India, one from the Reserve Bank of India, three from sponsoring State governments, three distinguished economists, three heads of sister research institutions, and members of other sponsoring agencies and invitees make up NIPFP's governing body.
 
• According to its website, the NIPFP was founded as an autonomous society under the Societies Registration Act, 1860, on the collaborative initiative of the Union Finance Ministry, the former Planning Commission, numerous state governments, and academicians.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Urjit Patel** is an Indian economist who previously served as the Reserve Bank of India's 24th Governor and also as its Deputy Governor, overseeing monetary policy, economic research, financial markets, statistics, and information management.
 
• **Krishnamurthy Venkata Subramanian **is a former Chief Economic Adviser to the Government of India. He was appointed to the role on December 7, 2018, and will leave on October 8, 2021. 
 
• **Kaushik Basu** is an Indian economist who served as the World Bank's Chief Economist from 2012 to 2016.
 
• **Arvind Subramanian **is an Indian economist who served as the Government of India's Chief Economic Advisor from 16 October 2014 to 20 June 2018.

questions.question: At which of the following places did C. Rajagopalachari break the salt law in the year 1930?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vedaranyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In British India, the Vedaranyam March (also known as the Vedaranyam Satyagraha)** was a framework for** nonviolent civil disobedience.**
 
• It was organised to protest **the salt tax **imposed by the British Raj in colonial India and was modelled after Mahatma Gandhi's Dandi March on the western coast of India the month before.
 
• Gandhi's close associate C. Rajagopalachari led the march, which drew close to 150 volunteers, most of whom were members of the Indian National Congress.
 
• It began on April 13, 1930, at Trichinopoly (now Tiruchirappalli) and went for around 240 kilometres east to Vedaranyam, a small coastal town in the Tanjore District. 
 
• When the participants were arrested by the colonial police force on April 28, 1930, the campaign came to an end.
 
• Rajagopalachari, the organization's leader, was sentenced to six months in prison.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Dandi march began the **Civil disobedience movement **when Gandhi left the Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad on foot with 78 other Ashram members towards Dandi on March 12, 1930.
 
• Gandhi disobeyed the salt prohibition after arriving in Dandi.

questions.question: Kwashiorkor disease occurs due to severe deficiency of _______ in the body.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**protein**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lack of protein **in the diet causes **Kwashiorkor**. Protein is found in every cell of the human body.
 
• Protein is needed in the human body's diet to repair and **regenerate cells.**
 
• This is how a healthy human body regenerates cells on a regular basis.
 
• Protein is particularly necessary for growth in children and during pregnancy.
 
• When the body is deficient in protein, growth and regular bodily functions slow down, and kwashiorkor develops.
 
• Proteins are in charge of keeping the body's fluid balance.
 
• Inadequate protein causes fluid to migrate to parts of the body where it shouldn't be, accumulating in the tissues.
 
• Fluid retention, often known as edoema, is caused by a fluid imbalance across the walls of capillaries. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **A protein** is an exceedingly complex natural molecule made up of amino acid residues linked by peptide bonds.
 
• Proteins are found in all living species and contain a variety of biologically important molecules such as enzymes, hormones, and antibodies.

questions.question: Where is Havelock Island, a popular tourist destination located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Andaman and Nicobar Islands**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Havelock Island **is located east of the **Andaman Islands **and is administered by the **Nicobar Islands administration.**
 
• It was named for** British General Henry Havelock**, who lived in the area when India was a British colony.
 
• Govinda Nagar, Krishna Nagar, Radha Nagar, Shyam Nagar, and Bejoy Nagar are five prominent settlements on Havelock Island, each with its own beaches and lovely shorelines.
 
• According to reports, the island is home to the majority of the island's immigrant population from Myanmar and Bengal.
 
• As a memorial to Subhash Chandra Bose, the island was renamed Swaraj Dweep in 2018.
 
• Subhash Chandra Bose flew the national flag on the island in 1943, naming Andaman Island Shaheed Dweep and Nicobar Island Swaraj Dweep, before India's independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• At the confluence of the **Bay of Bengal and the Andaman Sea**, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands are a union territory of India consisting of 572 islands, 37 of which are inhabited.
 
• The Andaman Sea separates the area from Thailand and Myanmar, around 150 kilometres north of Aceh, Indonesia.
 
• It is divided into two island groups, the Andaman Islands (partly) and the Nicobar Islands, by the 150-kilometre-long Ten Degree Channel, with the Andaman Islands to the north and the Nicobar Islands to the south.

questions.question: In which year were 30 Rigveda manuscripts dating from 1800 to 1500 BC included in the UNESCO's Memory of the World Register?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2007**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Rig Veda manuscripts** from **Pune's Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute **have been nominated for **UNESCO's 2007 "Memory of the World" Register.**
 
• In 2007, UNESCO added 30 Rigveda manuscripts to** the Memory of the World Register **at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute in Pune.
 
• Rigveda (Sanskrit: "Knowledge of Verses"), often spelled gveda, is the earliest of Hinduism's sacred scriptures, written in an ancient form of Sanskrit around 1500 BCE in what is now India and Pakistan's Punjab area.
 
• Vyasa is said to be the compiler of the Vedas, who divided the four types of mantras into four Samhitas (Collections).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **The Rigveda** is a collection of Vedic Sanskrit hymns (sktas) from ancient India.
 
• It is one of the Vedas, a collection of four sacred Hindu writings (ruti).
 
• The Rigveda is the oldest Vedic Sanskrit text that has been discovered.
 
• Its early layers are among the oldest Indo-European texts still extant. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Each Veda** is made up of hymns written by several priest families. In addition, the **Rig-Veda** is divided into ten books known as Mandalas.
 
• **The first and tenth Mandalas** are the most recent and longest volumes, respectively.
 
• The second to seventh Mandalas are the oldest, but also the shortest, parts of the Rig-Veda. The age groups in the eighth and ninth volumes are mixed.

questions.question: For immunity against which of the following diseases is BCG vaccine given?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tuberculosis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Bacillus Calmette–Guérin vaccine** is a tuberculosis vaccine developed by** Bacillus Calmette–Guérin.**
 
• It was created by **Albert Calmette and Camille Guérin** and is named after them. In nations where tuberculosis or leprosy are common, healthy neonates should receive one dose as soon as possible after delivery.
 
• **The WHO Expert Committee **on Biological Standardization first discussed the creation of worldwide requirements for the manufacture and control of BCG vaccine in its thirteenth report.
 
• The Committee requested that WHO make provisions as soon as possible for the drafting of such requirements in its fourteenth report.
 
• The WHO Expert Committee on Biological Standardization approved these requirements at its eighteenth meeting and included them as Annex 1 to its report. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Asthma** is a condition that causes your airways to narrow and swell, as well as create excess mucus.
 
• **The varicella vaccine, **often known as the chickenpox vaccine, is a chickenpox vaccination.
 
• Vaccinations against poliomyelitis are known as** polio vaccines**. A weakened poliovirus is administered by mouth and an inactivated poliovirus is delivered by injection.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a noble gas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Oxygen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Oxygen** is a colourless, odourless, and tasteless gas that is taken up by animals, which then convert it to carbon dioxide; plants, on the other hand, use carbon dioxide as a carbon source and return oxygen to the environment.
 
• Oxygen produces compounds when it reacts with nearly every other element, as well as when it reacts with other elements to displace them from their combinations; in many circumstances, these reactions are accompanied by the evolution of heat and light and are referred to as combustions.
 
• Water is the most crucial component.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Neon** is a chemical element with the atomic number 10 and the symbol Ne. It's classified as a noble gas.
 
• **Krypton **is an **atomic number 36** chemical element with the **symbol Kr.**
 
• **Argon **is a chemical element in the periodic table's eighteen groups. It is an **atomic number 18** and the **symbol Ar.** 
 
 
• It is the third most abundant gas in the earth's atmosphere and is a noble gas.

questions.question: Which of the following vitamins is also called 'cyanocobalamin'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vitamin B-12**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The mineral cobalt** is present in **cyanocobalamin (commonly known as Vitamin B12)**, which is a very complex, important vitamin.
 
• This vitamin, which is produced naturally by bacteria, is required for DNA synthesis and the creation of cellular energy.
 
• The cyano-, methyl-, deoxyadenosyl-, and hydroxy-cobalamin forms of vitamin B12 are among the many available.
 
• In supplements and pharmaceutical medications, the cyano form is the most common.
 
• Cyanocobalamin is available in a variety of pharmacological formulations, including tablets, injections, and nasal sprays.
 
• **Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) is a water-soluble vitamin** that aids in metabolism. It's one of the B vitamins, which are made up of eight different types. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Thiamine, often known as thiamin or vitamin B1**, is an important element that the body cannot produce. It's a dietary supplement or drug that's found in food and commercially synthesised.
 
• **Vitamin B6** (chemical name**- Pyridoxine-**4,5-Bis(hydroxymethyl)-2-methylpyridin-3-ol**)** is an essential ingredient because it is one of the B vitamins. The term "vitamers" refers to a collection of six chemically related molecules that can be interconverted in biological systems.
 
• **Niacin, **commonly known as nicotinic acid, is an organic molecule and a type of **vitamin B3** that is necessary for human health. 
 
• Vitamin B12 aids in the formation of DNA and red blood cells. Pernicious anaemia is a type of anaemia that makes it difficult for the human body to absorb vitamin B12.

questions.question: Who among the following is the chairman of NITI Aayog?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Narendra Modi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Narendra Modi **is **the chairman of NITI Aayog.**
 
• **The NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) **is the Government of India's apex public policy think tank and the nodal agency tasked with catalysing economic development and fostering cooperative federalism through bottom-up participation of State Governments in the economic policy-making process.
 
• The NDA government established it in 2015 to replace the Planning Commission, which operated on a top-down paradigm.
 
• All state Chief Ministers, as well as the Chief Ministers of Delhi and Puducherry, Lieutenant Governors of all UTs, and a vice-chairman appointed by the Prime Minister, make up the NITI Aayog council.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Narendra Damodardas Modi** is an Indian politician who has been the country's fourteenth and current Prime Minister since 2014. Modi served as Gujarat's chief minister from 2001 to 2014 and is a Varanasi Member of Parliament.
 
• **Rajiv Kumar** is an Indian economist who previously served as the NITI Aayog's second vice-chairman.
 
• **Amitabh Kant **is the second and current chief executive officer of NITI Aayog, the government of India's public policy think tank.
 
• **Nirmala Sitharaman** is an Indian politician and economist who has served as India's Minister of Finance and Corporate Affairs since 2019.

questions.question: What does the letter 'V' stand for in HVJ pipeline, which is India's first inter-state inland natural gas pipeline?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vijaipur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur (HVJ) pipeline** is **India's first cross-state gas pipeline.**
 
• The project began in 1986, with the **formation of GAIL (India)** Limited, with the goal of supplying gas to fertiliser facilities in Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The project's first phase, consisting of a 1,750-kilometer non-branched grid, was completed in 1987.
 
• The addition of new branches to supply gas for industrial and home usage across Rajasthan, Haryana, and the National Capital Territory, brings the overall grid length to 3,474 kilometers.
 
• **Indraprastha Gas Limited**, a newly formed company, gained control of the Delhi branch of the pipeline in 1998 in order to construct a citywide gas system.
 
• It has branches in Rajasthan's Kota, Uttar Pradesh's Shahajahanpur, Babrala, and other cities. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **GAIL Limited**, based in GAIL Bhawan in New Delhi, India, is a government-owned natural gas explorer and producer responsible for natural gas processing and distribution in India.
 
• It is owned by the Indian government's Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.

questions.question: Who among the following Sikh spiritual gurus is said to have assisted Khusro, the rebellious son of Jahangir?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Guru Arjun Dev**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Guru Arjun Dev, the fifth Sikh Guru**, had offered refuge to Prince Khusrau, who had risen against his father Jahangir.
 
• In 1606 AD**, Mughal emperor Jahangir** sentenced Guru Arjun Dev to death for bestowing his blessings on his rebel son and refusing to delete all Islamic and Hindu references from the Holy book, Guru Granth Sahib.
 
• **Guru Arjan** was the first of the two Sikh Gurus to be martyred, and the fifth of the ten Gurus in total.
 
• He created the Adi Granth, the first official edition of Sikh scripture, which was later extended into the Guru Granth Sahib.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Guru Angad** was the **second** of Sikhism's ten Sikh gurus.
 
• **Guru Ram Das** was the **fourth** of Sikhism's ten Gurus.
 
• **Guru Amar Das,** the **third** of Sikhism's Ten Gurus, became Sikh Guru on March 26, 1552, at the age of 73.
 
• The **first **and** tenth (last)** of Sikhism ten Sikh gurus are respectively **Guru Nanak** and** Guru Govind Singh**.

questions.question: The mineral Carnotite is an important source of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__U__**__**ranium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **K₂(UO₂)₂(VO₄)₂.3H₂O** is the chemical formula for **carnotite, a potassium uranium vanadate radioactive mineral.**
 
• Carnotite is made up of** roughly 53% uranium, 13% vanadium, **and trace quantities of radium.
 
• It was generated by alteration of primary uranium-vanadium minerals and is of secondary origin.
 
• It's commonly found in sandstone with tyuyamunite, either diffused or as small pure masses, especially around fossil wood.
 
• Carnotite was mined for vanadium and radium from 1911 to 1923 and produced the majority of uranium output from secondary deposits. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Uranium** is a silvery-white metallic chemical element with **atomic number 92 **in the periodic table.
 
• The chemical symbol for it is **U.**
 
• **Copper** is a chemical element with the** atomic number 29** and the symbol **Cu.**
 
• **Zinc** is a chemical element with the** atomic number 30** and the symbol **Zn**.
 
• At room temperature, zinc is a slightly brittle metal with a silvery-greyish look when oxidation is removed.
 
• The chemical element** iron** has the symbol **Fe** and the **atomic number 26. **
